desc:
You must complete every task in tasks, where tasks[i] = [duration, deadline]. You begin working at some integer time S ≥ 0, then work without any break, one task at a time in an order you choose, and no task is interrupted. Every task must finish at or before its deadline.

Return the largest start time S for which this is still possible, or -1 if even starting at time 0 is not enough.

tasks = [[3, 10], [2, 6]]  ->  4
tasks = [[5, 4]]           ->  -1

In the first example start at 4: the second task ends at 6 (deadline 6) and the first ends at 9 (deadline 10). Starting at 5 would make the second task end at 7.
hints: First fix the order. For a given order, each task gives an upper bound on S: S + (work up to and including it) ≤ deadline.
The best order is the one that makes the tightest of those bounds as loose as possible. Think about which task should come first.
Sort by deadline. The answer is the minimum over all tasks of deadline - (prefix sum of durations), or -1 when that minimum is negative.
editorial: With tasks done back to back in a fixed order, task i ends at S + P_i where P_i is the sum of the durations up to and including it. So the start time is limited by S ≤ deadline_i - P_i for every task, and the largest valid S is the minimum of these slacks.

Sorting by deadline (earliest first) maximizes that minimum slack, by the same exchange argument that makes earliest-deadline-first optimal for feasibility: moving a task with a later deadline in front of one with an earlier deadline can only shrink the slack of the earlier one. If the minimum slack is negative no start time works, so the answer is -1. Time O(n log n).
